The Shadow of the Collapse

When the structure of reality fractured, it did not simply leave behind empty space.

It left behind instability.

In places where the systems that once held the world together are damaged or missing, something else begins to grow.

This force is known as Darkness.

Darkness is not merely evil or malice.
It is the natural result of a broken system — the spreading disorder that appears when harmony fails.

Where the Great Work seeks to repair the world, Darkness spreads through the cracks left behind by the Collapse.

What Darkness Is

Darkness is a form of metaphysical corruption that weakens the balance of the world.

It appears when:

• communities collapse
• suffering spreads unchecked
• corruption takes root
• the structure of reality becomes unstable

In such places, the world begins to change in disturbing ways.

Landscapes become hostile.
Creatures behave unpredictably.
Strange phenomena appear that defy natural laws.

Darkness feeds on instability and makes broken places worse.

How Darkness Spreads

Darkness rarely arrives all at once.

Instead, it spreads gradually.

A struggling settlement might fall into despair.
A neglected region may become dangerous.
A powerful force may exploit the instability of a fractured hex.

Over time these small failures accumulate, allowing Darkness to grow stronger.

Left unchecked, it can transform entire regions of the world.

The Effects of Darkness

Regions touched by Darkness often show signs of deep imbalance.

These may include:

• corrupted environments
• hostile creatures emerging from unstable reality
• distorted natural systems
• communities collapsing under pressure

Darkness rarely destroys a place outright.

Instead, it warps what already exists, twisting the natural systems of the world.

Darkness and the Great Work

The Great Work exists partly to resist the spread of Darkness.

When factions stabilize hexes, help communities, and restore damaged systems, they weaken the conditions that allow Darkness to grow.

Every repaired region pushes back against corruption.

Every neglected region allows it to spread.

The struggle between restoration and decay is one of the defining forces shaping the age.

In Simple Terms

Darkness is the corruption that spreads when the broken world remains unstable.

It thrives in neglected places and feeds on disorder.

The Great Work seeks to contain it by repairing the systems that once held reality together.

Radiation

The Scars of a Broken World

The Collapse damaged more than the metaphysical structure of reality.

In many places, the physical world itself was altered by the forces released during the fracture.

One of the most dangerous remnants of that event is known as Radiation.

Radiation represents areas where the energy released by the Collapse still lingers, warping the environment and making survival difficult.

What Radiation Is

Radiation is a lingering environmental hazard caused by the instability of the world’s broken structure.

Unlike Darkness, which spreads through social and metaphysical imbalance, radiation represents physical damage to the environment itself.

Radiation may appear in many forms:

• invisible energy fields
• corrupted terrain
• unstable magical currents
• areas where the natural laws of the world behave unpredictably

These regions are often dangerous to enter and difficult to stabilize.

Where Radiation Appears

Radiation is most commonly found in places where the Collapse tore the structure of reality most violently.

These areas may include:

• shattered ruins of ancient infrastructure
• unstable wilderness regions
• locations where powerful forces were unleashed
• fragments of the world that never fully stabilized

Explorers often discover radiation zones while investigating previously unknown hexes.

The Effects of Radiation

Radiation can cause many different problems for travelers and communities.

These effects may include:

• environmental hazards that harm those who pass through
• unstable ecosystems where normal life struggles to survive
• strange mutations in creatures or plant life
• unpredictable magical phenomena

Because of these dangers, radiation zones often become barriers that slow exploration and development.

Overcoming Radiation

Although radiation zones are dangerous, they are not always permanent.

Through careful exploration, technological effort, and coordinated faction activity, some radiation zones can be stabilized.

Doing so is often an important step toward reclaiming damaged regions of the world.

Removing or reducing radiation allows communities to return and infrastructure to be rebuilt.

Radiation and Exploration

Radiation zones often hide important discoveries.

Ancient ruins, lost technology, and remnants of the world before the Collapse are frequently found in these unstable regions.

Because of this, explorers are often forced to choose between safety and discovery.

Many of the greatest secrets of the world remain hidden within places too dangerous for ordinary travelers.

In Simple Terms

Radiation represents the physical scars left behind by the Collapse.

These unstable regions make exploration dangerous but often contain valuable discoveries.

Stabilizing radiation zones is one of the many challenges factions must overcome while rebuilding the world.
